newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha off as Sonatrach blocks large cargoes.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha off as Sonatrach blocks large cargoes.

text.p: NWE naphtha was slightly weaker on Thursday as negative sentiment related to Algerian oil state oil company Sonatrach's block on the loading of large naphtha cargoes at Skikda weighed on the market, traders said.
May swaps were talked around the $177.50/$178.50 level, up from earlier levels around $176.50/$178 but $1 below Wednesday levels.
A player was heard bidding for pipeline spec at $179 but the closest offer was around $181.
Price levels for lower than 65 min paraffins material were assessed to be in the lower $170s on a cif NWE basis.
Traders said news Sonatrach was not giving permission for the loading of double stem May naphtha cargoes at Skikda had dampened market sentiment.
Sources who had spoken to the company said the suspension was due to the fact jetty three, the only one suitable for loading large cargoes, was being used to load fuel oil over the next 10 days.

The move would hit lifters hoping to move large cargoes Eastward, traders said. Some said the suspension could weigh on European prices if potential exporters to the East decided to keep material in Europe.
According to traders, one 60,000 tonne vessel was waiting to load an April double stem, while at least two May double stems had been in the pipeline.
"The April double stem will be loaded, but so far Sonatrach has refused to give permission for double stem loading in May," said one trader.
A number of players said, however, that despite the double stem block very little of the Skikda material was likely to stay in Europe.

"The stuff will still go East," said trader. "The spread's currently around $29-$32 and these guys still have to cover their shorts out there. Sure the suspension costs the lifters money but it won't change the arb situation."
"If somebody offered me a cargo of Algerian naphtha I would jump at it but the fact is it's not on offer in Europe," he added. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
